seo.title: How We Run on AI | M20 Technology
seo.description: How M20 embeds AI in its own operations: a custom Forge app, Rovo agent workflows, self-maintaining knowledge, and the governance that keeps it accountable.

hero.title: AI, built into how we work — not bolted on.
hero.intro: We don't just help clients apply AI across the Atlassian ecosystem — we run our own operations on it. This is a look at how AI is embedded in our billing operations, our workflows, our knowledge base, and the guardrails that keep it all accountable.

forge.title: From scattered billing ops to one app embedded in Jira.
forge.background: Billing for our own services and licenses ran on a patchwork of Jira automations, external scripts, and manual steps. We aren't an app-building business — our only app experience was building legacy Data Center apps — but invoicing and quoting volume had grown steadily for years, and Jira was already the hub tracking all of it. The result was an invoicing system cluttered with multiple draft estimates and invoices for the same deal.
forge.solution: We used Claude Code with Forge MCP to build a custom app embedded directly in our Jira instance. Plugging in the Teamwork Graph CLI and Rovo MCP feeds the app context straight from Jira tasks and related knowledge, and a Claude agent built into the Jira workflow can make code changes directly from the board.

workflows.title: Agents that work inside existing processes, not around them.
workflows.intro: Rather than standing up new tools, we plugged agents directly into the workflow steps we already had — creating, reviewing, and handing off work without giving anyone something new to learn.

cards.title: Recurring task creation
cards.text: A Rovo agent scans Confluence process docs daily and creates matching work items — assignees, details, and even fuzzy recurrences like "every odd year."

cards.title: AI intake
cards.text: An agent reads invoice PDFs and populates the matching work item directly — faster intake, fewer manual entry errors.

cards.title: Review
cards.text: A second agent checks items like bills and invoices for common errors before they move forward, catching problems earlier.

cards.title: Handoff
cards.text: Agents watch work-item status and hand off automatically, updating status and assignee so the next step starts itself.

knowledge.title: Knowledge that maintains itself.
knowledge.intro: We moved wiki maintenance from a manual chore to a standing agent job.

governance.title: Guardrails that scale with the agents.
governance.intro: More agents means more surface area — so governance is built in, not bolted on afterward.
items: **Documented agent best practices** — covering both development and testing
**A central agent registry** — so every agent in production is accounted for
**An audit agent** — compares our policies against actual implementation and generates an audit report plus Jira tasks for any gaps
**An Atlassian AI security guide** — the same guide we share with clients
